Journal: Spectrochimica Acta Part A: Molecular and Biomolecular Spectroscopy
Title: Structural, optical and electrical properties of Zr-doped In2O3 thin films
Abstract summary: Spray-pyrolyzed Zr-doped In2O3 films on glass (450 C, 0-11 at.% Zr) retained cubic structure; the abstract reports grain size decreasing from 25 to 15.75 nm, optical band gap decreasing from 3.50 to 3.0 eV, and a best resistivity of 6.4e-4 ohm·cm with carrier concentration 2.5e20 cm^-3 at 7 at.% Zr.
Keywords: spray pyrolysis; optical bandgap; resistivity; carrier concentration

Title: The Effect of Zirconium Doping on Solution-Processed Indium Oxide Thin Films Measured by a Novel Nondestructive Testing Method (Microwave Photoconductivity Decay)
Abstract summary: Solution-processed InxZryO thin films with Zr:In = 0, 5, 10, and 15 at.% were studied with post-anneals from 250 to 400 C. Zr doping improved crystallinity and density; the conclusions report a minimum oxygen vacancy fraction of 26.09% at 10 at.% Zr after annealing at 400 C.
Keywords: solution processing; Zr concentration; oxygen vacancies; mu-PCD

Title: Highly Conductive and Broadband Transparent Zr-Doped In2O3 as Front Electrode for Solar Cells
Abstract summary: A Zr-doped In2O3 transparent electrode for silicon heterojunction solar cells delivered wide band gap (3.5-4 eV), electron mobility of 100 cm^2/Vs, carrier density of 2.5-3e20 cm^-3, sheet resistance around 25 ohm/sq for 100 nm films, and device conversion efficiency of 23.4%.
Keywords: transparent electrode; band gap; mobility; solar cell

Journal: Progress in Photovoltaics: Research and Applications
Title: Highly conductive and broadband transparent Zr-doped In2O3 as the front electrode for monolithic perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells
Abstract summary: Room-temperature sputtered IZrO showed mobility of 29.6 cm^2/Vs, resistivity of 3.32e-4 ohm·cm, sheet resistance of 25.55 ohm/sq, average transmittance of 81.55% from 400-1200 nm, work function of 4.33 eV, and champion tandem efficiency of 28.28%.
Keywords: work function; broadband transparency; tandem solar cell; sputtering

Journal: Solar Energy Materials and Solar Cells
Title: Zirconium doped indium oxide thin films as transparent electrodes for photovoltaic applications
Abstract summary: Ultra-thin IZrO films grown at room temperature by RF co-sputtering (15-90 nm, 0.6-0.9 at.% Zr) and annealed at 200 C became more crystalline; the thinnest film reached resistivity of 5e-4 ohm·cm, mobility of 20 cm^2/Vs, and transmittance up to 80%, while 90 nm films gave EQE comparable to standard ITO.
Keywords: RF co-sputtering; ultra-thin films; EQE; photovoltaic
